Agent-facing code for [vaelii](https://github.com/vaelii/vaelii): an MCP server over a
Vaelii KB, clients for the model providers, and the KB read tools a model calls,
generated from the engine daemon's op table. The engine holds no AI-, model- or
protocol-specific code; this artifact does.

| namespace | what it holds |
|-----------|---------------|
| `vaelii.agents.mcp.server` | the MCP server's production entry point: startup ordering, custody checks, wiring |
| `vaelii.agents.mcp.verbs` | the six MCP verb tools (`assert`, `unassert`, `unassert_handle`, `query`, `argue`, `matching`) a client writes a fork KB through |
| `vaelii.agents.mcp.dispatcher` | transport-neutral JSON-RPC dispatch, the durable audit sink, and effect fencing |
| `vaelii.agents.mcp.session` | the session/fork/authority registry: durable, linearizable revocation and lease expiry |
| `vaelii.agents.mcp.audit` | pure v1 audit-record construction, validation, normalization and hashing |
| `vaelii.agents.mcp.config` | the EDN server-config reader: bearer-token fingerprints to principal/fork identity |
| `vaelii.agents.mcp.transport` | the stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 transport |
| `vaelii.agents.mcp.http-transport` | the Streamable HTTP transport and a raw-operation route |
| `vaelii.agents.mcp.overlay` | an optional directory of extra knowledge loaded into the base KB at server start |
| `vaelii.agents.llm.protocol` | the `Provider` protocol (`complete`, `stream`) and the neutral request and response maps |
| `vaelii.agents.llm.provider` | backend selection by keyword, lazily resolved, with the stub as the fallback |
| `vaelii.agents.llm.stub` | the deterministic, offline default provider, scripted per turn |
| `vaelii.agents.llm.anthropic` | the Messages API backend |
| `vaelii.agents.llm.ollama` | the local backend, over Ollama's chat API |
| `vaelii.agents.llm.http` | the transport policy both HTTP backends share: deadlines, bounded error bodies |
| `vaelii.agents.llm.pool` | a fixed pool of providers across hosts, and a majority yes/no vote over it |
| `vaelii.agents.tools` | the model's read tools: schemas generated from the daemon's read ops, and `call`, which dispatches a tool call back through them |
| `vaelii.agents.engine` | the engine vars outside `vaelii.core` that this repo reads, all in one namespace |

[docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md) documents the MCP server: the verbs, the transports, the
audit journal and the session/fork model. [docs/llm.md](docs/llm.md) documents the model
providers and the read tools: the environment variables and the refusal `:type`s.

## Using it

Leiningen `[com.vaelii/vaelii-agents "0.33.0"]`, or deps.edn
`com.vaelii/vaelii-agents {:mvn/version "0.33.0"}`, from
[Clojars](https://clojars.org/com.vaelii/vaelii-agents). It depends on the engine at the
version it was cut with, so a project naming only this one gets both.

```clojure
(require '[vaelii.agents.llm.provider :as provider]
         '[vaelii.agents.tools :as tools])

(def p (provider/provider))   ; VAELII_LLM_PROVIDER's backend, or the stub
(tools/schemas)               ; the tool definitions to send with a request
(tools/call kb "kb_query" {"goal" "(dog ?x)" "context" "CxUniverse"})
;; => {:ok true :result "…"}
```

No tool writes. The tool set is the daemon's read ops minus every op that stores, holds
the writer, names a path on the host or reads with no bound a call can carry (docs/llm.md
§ Tools).

## Layout for a new component

A component that connects the engine to an agent (a protocol server, an agent runtime's
adapter) goes in its own namespace tree, `vaelii.agents.<component>.*`, with its tests
under `test/vaelii/agents/<component>/` and its page at `docs/<component>.md`. An MCP
server, for instance, is `vaelii.agents.mcp.*`. A component reuses `vaelii.agents.tools`
for KB reads where the generated tools fit, and writes its own handlers where they do not.

**Reaching into the engine.** The engine's public API is `vaelii.core`. A component may
call `vaelii.host.*` too, as `vaelii.agents.tools` does, and the engine is free to change
that namespace tree in any release. Route each such call through
`vaelii.agents.engine`, so an engine change is repaired in one namespace. A read the
public API lacks and every caller would want belongs in `vaelii.core`, proposed upstream.

A component's own dependencies go in `project.clj` with a comment naming the namespace
that needs them.

## Setup

```sh
lein test
```

The engine resolves from Clojars, so a fresh clone needs nothing else. Working against
an **unreleased** engine, a snapshot `com.vaelii/vaelii` comes out of `~/.m2`:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vaelii/vaelii ../vaelii
cd ../vaelii && lein install
cd -          && lein test
```

Working against live engine source instead of the installed jar:

```sh
./scripts/link-checkouts.sh   # checkouts/vaelii -> the engine beside this repo
```

Every KB the suite builds is on the engine's in-memory backend, so `lein test` runs beside
the engine's own suite. No test calls a model: the stub answers every turn.

## Development

```
lein lint          → versions + kondo + shellcheck + cljfmt + reflection + prose, not fail-fast
lein fix           → the only auto-repair: cljfmt rewrites in place
lein gate          → lint, then the suite; run this before opening a pull request
lein test :llm     → only the tests marked ^:llm, which call a model when VAELII_LLM_LIVE=1
```

`lein lint` needs `clj-kondo` and `shellcheck` on PATH. The reflection stage AOT-compiles
`src` under `*warn-on-reflection*` and fails on any warning from this repo's own code.

`scripts/update-badges.sh` measures the repo and rewrites the badge block under the H1,
fetching each badge from shields.io. Do not hand-edit the block.
